main_body: stone tower with a conical tiled roof
top_band: greenish-teal tiled conical roof slope from rows 3 to 39 (with gold finial at rows 0-3), followed by a brown eave trim at rows 40-41
evidence: The structure clearly displays its top conical roof surface (rows 3-39) above the vertical stone wall face (rows 42-95). A brown trim marks the front edge at rows 40-41, casting an eave shadow onto row 42. The window and door on the front face have recessed dark inner edges.

style.evidence: While the roof has a decent 6-step ramp and tiled pattern, the stone walls are built from large, completely flat rectangular blocks (~6x4 pixels of solid color with no internal grain or per-stone shading), and the wooden door planks and window panes are flat fills. Compared to the Beodeul stone house reference (which shades every small stone individually and speckles plaster), the candidate has much lower tile information density and reads as flat.
